questions.question: An Exile takes the Oathkeeper title during their Act phase. When can they first win as Usurper, and what happens if someone takes the title away meanwhile?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: At their next Wake they check victory before flipping Oathkeeper to Usurper, so cannot yet win as Usurper; if still Usurper at the following Wake they win. Losing the title prevents this; a new holder receives it Oathkeeper-side. At end of round eight an existing Usurper can win under the ordered endgame rules.

required_facts.expected_fact: Victory is checked before the next-Wake Oathkeeper-to-Usurper flip; ordinary Usurper victory is at the following Wake if retained.
An existing Usurper can instead win at the end-of-round-eight priority check, potentially before the following Wake.
Losing the title prevents that win; transfer/retaking uses the Oathkeeper side and restarts the sequence.

questions.semantic_notes: Preserves established seed requested scope; equivalent unambiguous meaning accepted, no cross-question borrowing.

reader-a.answer: The Exile cannot win as Usurper in the same Act. At their next Wake, they first check for victory while still Oathkeeper; then, if still holding title, flip it to Usurper. Their first Usurper win check is the following Wake, unless round 8 ends first while they remain Usurper. Losing the title prevents the win; retaking it resets the title to Oathkeeper and restarts the sequence.

scenario.given_state: An Exile takes the Oathkeeper title during their Act.
scenario.completed_events: The title transfer has happened during Act; that turn’s Wake is already over.
scenario.next_operation: At the Exile’s next Wake check victory, then flip to Usurper if still titleholder.
scenario.result: First ordinary Usurper victory check is the following Wake; loss of title prevents it, and retaking resets the sequence.

reader-b.answer: Taking Oathkeeper in Act does not make the Exile Usurper immediately. At next Wake, check occurs before title flips; first Usurper check is the following Wake, or round 8 if earlier. Losing title prevents the win; retaking resets Oathkeeper-side.

scenario.given_state: An Exile takes the Oathkeeper title during Act.
scenario.completed_events: The title was just taken during the current Act.
scenario.next_operation: At next Wake check wins before title flips; after flip, check on later Wake (unless round 8 arrives first).
scenario.result: First Usurper win opportunity is following Wake or round-eight end if still Usurper; losing title blocks it and retaking resets sequence.

Draw the prescribed three, or all available if source runs out, except when a world Vision stops drawing or a modifier changes count; from world one at a time, announce a Vision, stop immediately and increment track; discard Vision does neither. Discard all but one before playing or discarding that one.

Discard costs two; world costs two at zero Visions, three at one/two, four at three–five, subject to modifiers including Darkest Secret’s fixed two.

Draw the prescribed three unless depletion, a world Vision or modifier changes/stops the count; draw world cards one at a time, announce that a Vision was drawn, stop immediately and advance the shared track.
Discard Vision neither stops draw nor advances track.

reader-a.answer: Search chooses either the world deck or the discard pile for your pawn’s region, never both. Discard Search costs 2 Supply. World Search costs 2 at 0 Visions drawn, 3 at 1–2, or 4 at 3–5; Darkest Secret makes world Search cost 2, with other modifiers still applying. Draw 3, fewer only if source runs out, a world Vision stops the draw, or a modifier reduces it; you cannot stop voluntarily. A world-deck Vision is announced, stops Search immediately, and advances the track by 1. A Vision drawn from discard neither stops the draw nor advances the track.

Facedown advisers lack suit/restriction banner/power; any card can be held facedown.

reader-a.answer: There may be up to 3 advisers total, counting faceup and facedown. Before exceeding the limit, discard an adviser if permitted; locks still apply. A facedown adviser has no suit, restriction, or power; any card, including site-only cards and Visions, may be held facedown. Later, a facedown adviser may be played faceup legally or discarded as a minor action; a faceup adviser cannot be discarded at will. Either banner from anywhere, even yourself: pay more favor/secrets than old amount, stack new payment. People’s Favor flips off Mob and old favor distributes singly along banks away from deck from any starting suit wrapping. Recover only facedown relic at pawn site at printed site cost; take faceup into personal bank.
Either banner from anywhere/self/shared bank: pay strictly more of appropriate resource than existing amount and replace old stack with payment.
People’s Favor returns off Mob; old favor distributes singly to banks starting with any suit, moving away from world deck, wrapping.
Darkest Secret new holder takes one old secret, previous holder gets rest; self gets all, bank remainder stays bank.

reader-a.answer: Recover costs 1 Supply plus target cost. A facedown relic must be at your site; pay its printed site cost and hold it faceup in your personal bank. Either banner can be recovered from anywhere (including you or shared bank). For People’s Favor, pay strictly more favor than it currently has, add payment to it, distribute its old favor one at a time through suit banks starting at a chosen bank, then flip Mob to normal; no seizure penalty applies. For Darkest Secret, pay strictly more secrets than it has, place them on it, take 1 old secret and give the rest to prior holder (if yourself, all old secrets return to you; shared-bank remainder stays there).

reader-b.answer: Recover relic: pay 1 Supply plus its printed cost, only for facedown relic at your site, then hold faceup. Banner anywhere including self/shared bank: strictly overbid its resources. For Darkest Secret, new holder takes one old secret and former holder takes rest; self takes all old back, shared remainder stays. No seizure penalty.

questions.question: How are Campaign attack/defense calculated, and how do skulls, hollow swords, ties and sacrifices work?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: The attacker may collect attack dice up to the number of warbands in their attacking force (normally those on their board), after accounting for any applicable power that changes that force. Then apply the appropriate dice modifiers. Defense shields multiplied by each double (x2,x4,...), plus warbands at targeted sites and defender board if pawn at attacker or targeted site; bandits one per targeted site. Attack skulls kill own force immediately; paired hollow swords count one, lone hollow zero. Attack must strictly exceed defense; may sacrifice force warbands +1 each, exactly enough to win, no excess; if unable/decline defender wins.
questions.source_references: Law 5.5.2,5.5.4–6,9.5; official errata Law5.5.2 attacking FORCE ceiling

required_facts.expected_fact: Attacker chooses dice up to warbands in force.
Defense is shields multiplied exponentially by doubles plus defending site warbands and board warbands only with pawn at attacker/targeted site; bandits one per targeted bandit site.
Skulls immediately kill own force warbands; full swords count, paired hollow swords add one, lone hollow adds zero.
